title: Introduce atomic presubmit profiles and dep-detangler to reduce premerge cost
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary: This PR introduces two complementary changes to reduce premerge CI cost and friction: 1) an atomic presubmit profiles system that picks a targeted set of lint/test steps based on the commit footprint and code ownership heuristics; 2) a lightweight dep-detangler that produces safe, minimal lockfile/upgrade patches for large JS/TS dependency trees to avoid noise from monolithic lockfile churn.

Motivation: Our presubmit lanes run a lot of unrelated work for small edits which increases queue time and expenditure. Lockfile churn from bulk automated upgrades has caused a number of flaky presubmits and long CI runs during release windows.

Design:
- Presubmit profiles: introduce a YAML-based profiles manifest (ci/presubmit/profiles.yaml) and a small coordinator (scripts/ci/presubmit_profile_router.py) that selects which checks to run: quick-lint, unit-fast, integration-light, e2e-nightly, and docs-only. Selection heuristics combine file globs, CODEOWNERS hints, and a change-size threshold. Profiles are additive and declarative so maintainers can opt-in per package.
- Dep-detangler: a CLI utility (tools/dep_detangler) that analyzes package.json+lockfile, computes a minimal upgrade or lockfile delta needed to satisfy a target vulnerability or required bump, and emits a sanitized patch and summary. It uses a strategy of isolating direct dep changes and pinning transient upgrades behind an opt-in label so CI runs remain stable.

Non-goals: This PR does not change production runtime dependencies or alter the hosted release pipeline; it focuses on CI optimization and repo hygiene only.

Checklist:
- [x] Add presubmit profiles manifest and router
- [x] Wire GitHub Action inputs to run a profile-detection step early in the workflow
- [x] Add dep-detangler prototype and a wrapper GH Action
- [x] Add tests for profile selection heuristics and detangler sim scenarios
- [x] Document usage in docs/dev/ci.md
- [x] Smoke test on redwood/sdk-ts and redwood/redwood-docs

How to validate locally: run `python scripts/ci/presubmit_profile_router.py --files <changed-files>` to see selected profile; run `tools/dep_detangler/bin/detangle --pkg packages/sdk-ts/package.json --target 2.1.0` to generate a patch.

Commits summary:
- feat(ci): add presubmit profiles manifest and selection router
- feat(tooling): initial dep-detangler CLI + GH Action wrapper
- test(ci): add fixture sets for profile routing and detangler scenarios
- ci(workflow): wire profile-detection as an early job and conditionalize subsequent jobs
- docs: add dev guide and examples

The changed areas (high level):
- .github/workflows/presubmit.yaml: add early profile-detection job and conditional job matrix
- ci/presubmit/profiles.yaml: profiles manifest with globs and thresholds
- scripts/ci/presubmit_profile_router.py: deterministic router logic and unit tests
- tools/dep_detangler/: CLI prototype, tests, small parser
- packages/sdk-ts/: example integration and CI config tweaks
- docs/dev/ci.md: new developer docs and example runbook

Review conversation (abridged):
- Miguel Romero (2026-02-21): "Nice approach. Two concerns: 1) how do we avoid profiles diverging (i.e. silent bypass of critical checks)? 2) detangler could hide necessary transitive updates. Can we add a safety net that forces full presubmit for CRs touching core infra files?"
- Asha Patel (2026-02-22): "Agree. Added a protected set (ci/presubmit/always_run_globs.yaml) that forces full lanes for critical paths (build scripts, infra, release hooks). Dep-detangler also emits a 'safety_score' and will block automatic patching if the score < 0.7; in that case a maintainer review is required."
- Evelyn Chen (2026-02-24): "I ran the router against a recent monorepo PR and selected 'unit-fast + quick-lint' as expected. Two nits in tests assert order dependence; suggest making them order-agnostic."
- Asha Patel (2026-02-25): "Fixed by sorting profiles in the selection result and adding a deterministic seed for file list processing."
- Lucas Meyer (2026-02-27): "CI flaked on a node 16 vs 18 matrix; dep-detangler produced a minor range bump that wasn't compatible with node 16. Recommend adding node-version guard in detangler report."
- Asha Patel (2026-02-28): "Added node-version check and an opt-in flag `--allow-node-range-bump`. Also added a fast-path in the GH Action to run full-lane when matrix targets differ."

CI run history summary:
- initial run (2026-02-23): presubmit profile detection job passed; unit-fast failed due to test ordering in router tests
- rerun after tests fixed (2026-02-25): all selected jobs passed but detangler integration step timed out on a heavy fixture
- timeout investigated; added incremental timeout and stream logs (2026-02-26)
- final run (2026-02-28): green across matrix after adding node-version guard and increasing detangler timeout

Release notes / impact:
- Introduces new CI behavior: small PRs will run a targeted subset of checks, improving feedback time.
- Adds tools/dep_detangler to aid safe dependency updates and reduce noisy lockfile churn.
- Repo maintainers should review profiles.yaml and the always-run globs to ensure critical paths are covered.

Post-merge follow ups:
- Roll out profiles to a small set of active packages for two weeks, gather feedback (ENG-2341 follow-up)
- Add a lightweight dashboard to track how often profiles pick reduced lanes and any false negatives
- Iterate on detangler heuristics and add support for pnpm workspaces (ENG-2342)

Merge outcome: Squash-merged after approvals from Miguel and Evelyn.

RFC/notes: This approach trades some presubmit coverage for faster iteration; the safety nets added (always_run_globs, safety_score thresholds, node-version guard) are intended to keep risk low. If we observe regressions, the quick rollback path is to disable profile-detection in the GH workflow and revert the detangler GH Action.
commits: feat(ci): presubmit profiles manifest and router
test(ci): add fixtures and unit tests
ci(workflow): wire profile-detection and conditional matrix
review_comments: Miguel Romero: Nice approach, please ensure critical paths always run full CI.
Evelyn Chen: Tests were flaky due to ordering; recommend deterministic sorting.
Lucas Meyer: Detangler caused node-range bump that broke node 16; add guard.
Asha Patel: Added always_run_globs, safety_score, node-version guard, and deterministic ordering.
notes: Prototype: detangler is intentionally conservative; it will not auto-apply patches if safety_score < 0.7.
Presubmit profiles are additive and can be opted-in per package by adding ci/presubmit/profiles.yaml entries.
This change reduces median presubmit wall-time for small edits in initial canary (sdk-ts) by ~42% in our tests.
